source_text:
Et tamen admonentur homines doctissimorum libris et carminibus poetarum illius ignei fluminis et de Stygia palude saepius ambientis ardoris, quae cruciatibus aeternis praeparata et daemonum indiciis et de oraculis profetarum cognita tradiderunt.
et ideo apud eos etiam ipse rex Iuppiter per torrentes ripas et atram uoraginem iurat religiose: destinatam enim sibi cum suis cultoribus poenam praescius perhorrescit.
nec tormentis aut modus ullus aut terminus. illic sapiens ignis membra urit et reficit, carpit et nutrit. sicut ignes fulminum corpora tangunt nec absumunt, sicut ignes Aetnaei montis et Vesuui montis et ardentium ubique terrarum flagrant nec erogantur: ita poenale illud incendium non damnis ardentium pascitur, sed inexesa corporum laceratione nutritur.
eos autem mento torqueri, qui lJeum nesciunt, ut impios, ut iniustos, nisi profanus nemo deliberat, cum parentem omnium et omnium dominum non minoris sceleris sit ignorare quam laedere.
et quamquam inperitia Dei sufficiat ad poenam, ita ut notitia prosit ad ueniam, tamen si uobiscum Christiani comparemur, quamuis in nonnullis disciplina nostra minor est, multo tamen uobis meliores deprehendemur.
uos enim adulteria prohibetis et facitis, nos uxoribus nostris solummodo uiri nascimur: uos scelera admissa punitis, apud nos et cogitare peccare est: uos conscios timetis, nos etiam conscientiam solam, sine qua esse non possumus: denique de uestro numero carcer exaestuat, Christianus ibi nullus nisi aut reus suae religionis aut profugus.
thought_title: The eternal fire and the moral comparison of Christians with pagans
orientation: Octavius is still replying to Caecilius, now describing the eternal punishment that awaits the wicked and then comparing Christian morals with pagan practice.
pass_a_gloss: And yet men are warned by the books of the most learned and by the songs of poets about that fiery river and about the burning heat of the Stygian marsh flowing around repeatedly, which things, prepared for eternal torments and known from the indications of demons and from the oracles of the prophets, they have handed down. And therefore among them even king Jupiter himself swears religiously by the torrent banks and the black abyss: for, foreknowing, he shudders at the punishment destined for himself along with his worshippers. Nor is there any limit or end to the torments. There the wise fire burns the limbs and restores them, plucks them and nourishes them. Just as the fires of lightning touch bodies and do not consume them, just as the fires of Mount Etna and Mount Vesuvius and of burning lands everywhere blaze and are not spent: so that penal fire is not fed by the losses of those burning, but is nourished by the un-eaten tearing of bodies. But that those who do not know God are tormented, as impious, as unjust, no one deliberates unless he is profane, since to be ignorant of the parent of all and the lord of all is a crime not less than to harm him. And although ignorance of God is enough for punishment, so that knowledge avails for pardon, nevertheless if we Christians are compared with you, although in some things our discipline is less, yet we will be found much better than you. For you forbid adulteries and commit them; we are born as men only for our wives: you punish crimes committed; among us even to think is to sin: you fear witnesses; we fear even conscience alone, without which we cannot exist: finally the prison swarms with your number; no Christian is there unless either accused of his own religion or a fugitive.

choices.why: Keeps the paradoxical personification of the fire as knowing how to punish without consuming, matching the Latin adjective.

choices.english: by the un-eaten tearing of bodies
choices.why: Preserves the literal paradox that the bodies are torn but not consumed, which is the point of the comparison with lightning and volcanic fire.
rejected: by the endless mangling of bodies
by the undevoured rending of bodies

choices.english: we are born as men only for our wives
choices.why: Renders the literal 'we are born men' with the dative of purpose 'for our wives', keeping the sexual exclusivity claim.
rejected: we are men only for our wives
we are born husbands only to our wives

choices.why: Keeps the vivid verb 'exaestuat' (boils over, swarms) rather than flattening to 'is full'.

choices.english: no one deliberates unless he is profane
choices.why: Keeps the double negative and the verb 'deliberat' (deliberates, doubts) rather than simplifying to 'no one doubts'.
rejected: no one doubts unless he is profane
only a profane person would doubt

pass_b_english: And yet people are warned by the books of the most learned men and by the poems of the poets about that river of fire and the burning heat that constantly surrounds the Stygian marsh. They have handed down that this fire is prepared for eternal torments, known both from the testimony of demons and from the oracles of the prophets.

That is why among them even King Jupiter himself swears religiously by the torrential banks and the black abyss. Foreknowing the punishment appointed for himself and his worshippers, he shudders at it.

Nor is there any limit or end to the torments. There the wise fire burns the limbs and restores them, tears them away and feeds them. Just as the fires of lightning touch bodies without consuming them, just as the fires of Mount Etna and Mount Vesuvius and of burning lands everywhere blaze without being spent, so that penal fire is not fed by the loss of what burns, but is nourished by the unending tearing of bodies.

But that those who do not know God are tormented as impious and unjust, no one deliberates unless he is profane, since to be ignorant of the parent and lord of all is no less a crime than to harm him.

And although ignorance of God is enough for punishment, just as knowledge avails for pardon, still if we Christians are compared with you, even though our discipline is inferior in some respects, we will nevertheless be found much better than you.

For you prohibit adulteries and commit them; we are born husbands solely for our wives. You punish crimes once committed; among us even to think of sin is to sin. You fear witnesses; we fear even our conscience alone, without which we cannot exist. Finally, the prison swarms with your number; no Christian is there unless he is accused of his religion or a fugitive.
notes: The source text has 'lJeum' with a capital J in the middle, likely OCR damage for 'Deum' (God); glossed as 'God'.

problems.quote: we are born as men only for our wives
problems.source_quote: nos uxoribus nostris solummodo uiri nascimur
problems.why: 'uiri nascimur' means 'we are born men/husbands,' i.e., we become husbands solely for our wives. 'As men only' changes meaning to suggest maleness rather than marital fidelity.
problems.fix: we are born husbands solely for our wives
problems.ruling: ‘uiri nascimur’ means ‘we are born husbands’, not just ‘as men’; gender vs marital role shift

edits.old: we are born as men only for our wives
edits.new: we are born husbands solely for our wives

fixed: Changed 'we are born as men only for our wives' to 'we are born husbands solely for our wives': source 'uiri nascimur' means 'we are born husbands/men' in the sense of becoming husbands, not maleness.

last_rejected.quote: no one deliberates unless he is profane
last_rejected.why: "deliberat" means "doubts/hesitates," not "deliberates"; "profanus" means "uninitiated/impious," not "profane" in modern sense.
last_rejected.fix: no one doubts this unless he is impious

last_rejected.quote: we are born husbands solely for our wives
last_rejected.source_quote: nos uxoribus nostris solummodo uiri nascimur
last_rejected.why: "nascimur" here means "are born/come into being as," but "solely" placement is awkward; better "we are born men only for our wives."
last_rejected.fix: we are born men only for our wives
last_rejected.ruling: uiri = ‘men’; ‘husbands’ is a contextual gloss, not a meaning change

last_rejected.quote: the prison swarms with your number
last_rejected.why: "exaestuat" means "boils over/is crammed full"; "swarms with your number" is unclear—should mean "your kind/people fill the prison to bursting."
last_rejected.fix: the prison boils over with your kind
last_rejected.ruling: exaestuat = ‘boils over, is crowded’; ‘swarms with your number’ conveys that

polish.changed: Clarified the paradoxical description of the penal fire, made the subject of the warning explicit, and smoothed sentence flow while preserving every claim and reference.

notes.why: 'Deity' and 'God' are used interchangeably but sometimes 'deity' refers to pagan gods, sometimes to the one God.
notes.fix: Distinguish pagan 'deities' from the one 'God' more consistently.

notes.quote: the wise fire burns and restores the limbs, plucks them and nourishes them
notes.why: Paradoxical fire that 'plucks and nourishes' is confusing; refers to eternal punishment's renewing destruction.
notes.fix: 'tears away and restores' with note on paradox.
